tasks.task: Write the program for one sensor, counter or display gadget

items.when: When the client has only a rough idea and you need scope and limits written before code
When the build uses tasks on an ESP32 or similar chip and memory and failure handling matter
When you write the sketch or script so it keeps reading, counting and showing without stalls
Before the client builds it, to confirm every library and board version really exists
When the program is drafted, to list the cases to try on the bench, smallest first
When the design has grown parts it does not need, to cut it to the fewest that do the job

tasks.task: Take a new gadget from brief to a working test

items.when: When a client asks for a new counter, logger, queue light, display or sensor alarm
When the build is more than one evening's work and needs small ordered steps with a check each
When the client needs to know what will be tested, at what level and what is left out
Before parts are ordered, to list how the plan could fail and what to change

tasks.task: Find why a board or script misbehaves and fix it

items.when: When you have the fault, the error and the code near it and need suspects ranked with a check each
When you have code, wiring notes, photos and output and need the likely cause and the fix
When earlier fixes did not hold and the cause must be proven before anything changes
When an AI tool keeps failing at the same fix and you need a three-try plan and a way back
When the code lives in a repository and the fix needs a test and a pull request
When guesses pile up, to follow what the code and the signal really do step by step

tasks.task: Triage a serial log from a board that resets or freezes

items.when: When a board resets, freezes or reads nonsense and you have the serial output
When the log is from a Pi script or service and holds a Python error or stack trace
When the log points at wiring or power and the code must be read beside it

tasks.task: Build a pin table and wiring guide

items.when: When a low-voltage gadget needs each pin, wire and part value written out plainly
When the guide needs a simple block picture of what connects to what
Before power-on, to check part limits with worst-case sums and plan staged bench tests
When resistor, current or divider sums must have units and margins checked

tasks.task: Check a circuit and power budget before power-on

items.when: When you have the real circuit and part sheets and need limits, sums and a bench plan
When wire sizes, supply ratings or standards need a second, checked calculation
When the check changes a pin or part and the table must be redone

tasks.task: Write a wiring and set-up README for a kit or gadget

items.when: When the gadget works and a customer or colleague must set it up without help
When buyers of a kit should understand the code, with each part beside its reason
When the project is a repository another developer will take over
When the README is drafted, to follow each step and mark it working or broken
When a step only makes sense to you, to explain it with a plain example a beginner follows

tasks.task: Set a Raspberry Pi script to start on boot with logs

items.when: When a script works by hand and must start on boot, restart on a crash and keep logs
When the script must finish a write or close a device cleanly when it is stopped
When part of the job runs on a cron line, to see its next run times and catch mistakes

tasks.task: Check libraries, cores and versions before a build

items.when: Before building someone else's project, upgrading a core, or trusting AI-written firmware
When a Pi project is Python and its libraries changed after the AI tool was trained
When a call looks made up and must be checked against the official docs, with sources
When a core or SDK jump could break the build and needs stages with a test each
When an AI wrote the firmware fast and you want the few risks that will hurt later
When a change needs a ranked review of bugs, tests and clarity
When the code uses libraries nobody has checked exist at that version
When one long loop must be split into small parts without changing what it does

tasks.task: Plan how a connected product gets firmware updates

items.when: When a product in other people's hands needs a safe way to receive each new release
When many devices are in the field, some offline, and stages and health checks are needed
Before trusting the update path, to plan failure tests and review the recovery evidence
When the plan assumes power and signal never drop mid-update, to design for when they do

tasks.task: Roll out a firmware change in stages

items.when: When a fix or feature is ready for devices other people own
When you need preflight checks, stage sizes and the health signals that stop the rollout
When owners need to know what changed in this version, from the commits
When an update went wrong and the lesson must change the procedure

tasks.task: List security and marking gaps before a product is sold

items.when: When a connected gadget is about to be sold and you need questions for the test lab
When it will be sold in the EU and you need its risk class, duties and reporting steps
When nobody has listed how the device, its app and its cloud could be attacked
When a buyer or rule asks for a software parts list and known weak packages
When a protection is proposed, to ask what it guards, what it costs and what stays open

tasks.task: List the parts and cost the build

items.when: When a kit or product needs a cost sheet by part with price-break questions
When one hard-to-get part could stall a batch and second sources are needed
When two or three boards could do the job and need a side-by-side with a pick

tasks.task: Log readings and show them on a simple dashboard

items.when: When the device must keep reading and saving on time while it also sends data
When readings go to an online service and the Pi needs sign-in, retries and error handling
When logged readings should become one offline page of charts the owner can open
When raw counts are turned into degrees, volts or litres and the sums need checking

tasks.task: Write a troubleshooting page for people who bought a kit

items.when: When one solved buyer problem should become a page with steps and what they should see
When many buyer questions need clear, searchable answers
When you first need the real causes behind the faults buyers report

tasks.task: Draft a simple mount or case for the board

items.when: When a bracket or simple case is needed as a printable file from key sizes
Before sizing the case, to know where each connector and cable leaves the board

always.when: Whenever you change a client's code, to ground each step in their real files and check it
At the end of any job, to write what changed, what was tested on real hardware and what was not

helpers.when: When the gadget is becoming a product: case, materials, makers and test lab
When devices need a server, an API or a database behind them
When a connected product needs a full review of its app, cloud and update path
When a kit needs a full printed manual, not one README
When the gadget needs a phone app to set it up or read it
When CE, UKCA, FCC or radio rules need an owner beyond a list of questions

gaps: The library is thin for this role's core work: most hardware items need MATLAB, so the items listed are mostly general coding, docs and release items
No library item writes an Arduino sketch, ESP32 program or Raspberry Pi script; only the kit does
No library item writes FreeRTOS or Zephyr tasks, queues and timers, or checks stack and heap use
No library item draws a wiring diagram or breadboard layout from a pin table
No library item works out a power budget or battery life for a small device
No library item helps choose a board, sensor or display for a job and a budget
No library item covers MQTT, Home Assistant, ESPHome or sending readings to a cloud dashboard
No library item covers Bluetooth or Wi-Fi set-up on a device without MATLAB
No library item writes host-side unit tests or a hardware-in-the-loop test for firmware
No library item filters or calibrates sensor readings in C or Python on the device
No library item covers CE, UKCA, FCC or radio approval steps for a small maker
No library item makes a case with cut-outs for a named board; the one design item is for lab parts
The case task has no item that offers different designs to compare or checks fit before printing
